Eleven years ago I was introduced to @a_zatarain about sponsoring a 20VC episode.

She did not know but this payment was used to pay for some of my mother’s MS treatment.

The partnership happened and a friendship blossomed between me, Alexandra and Matteo.

I remember 10 years ago, everyone thought they were crazy. Italian CEO, not an engineer, doing hardware with a supply chain in China. Haha, good luck.

How wrong they were. A multi-BN business today doing hundreds of millions in revenue.

An insanely fun chat with my friend @m_franceschetti 👇

1. How to Do Paid Marketing Really, Really Well

Disciplined paid marketing means scaling one channel at a time, starting with Meta, while maintaining a strict cap on customer acquisition cost (CAC). Overspending destroys unit economics and eventually forces pullbacks that hurt year-over-year growth. Holding firm on CAC today creates the foundation for predictable, compounding growth tomorrow.

2. The Story Behind How Eight Sleep Partnered With Charles Leclerc

The best partnerships come from authentic product adoption and long-term conviction. Eight Sleep tried to sponsor Charles Leclerc years before he reached F1. When they eventually met, Leclerc was already an unprompted Eight Sleep user, allowing a shared vision around AI and performance to turn into a partnership within days.

3. We Do $100 Million in Email Marketing With No Employees

Operational constraints can force breakthrough automation. When Eight Sleep’s email lead left, co-founder Alexandra built AI bots in three days to manage the entire workflow. Today, the channel operates with zero dedicated employees while generating nearly $100 million in revenue.

4. What Seems Crazy but Will Be Very Commonplace in Five Years’ Time?

Autonomous assets managed by personal AI agents could create entirely new forms of passive income. Within five years, an individual’s AI agent could buy an autonomous cybercab, manage its daily operations, and generate revenue with minimal human involvement.

5. Why Angel Investing as a Founder Has Taught Me So Much About Company Building

Angel investing can become a powerful market intelligence engine for active founders. Reading investor updates from non-competing startups provides real-time insight into valuation shifts, hiring profiles, and acquisition channels that are working, all of which can directly inform operating decisions.

6. With AI, Every Company Will Turn Into a Holding Company With Multiple Products

AI-powered internal tooling dramatically lowers the cost and friction of launching new ventures, allowing single-product startups to evolve into conglomerates. Like Chinese giants such as Xiaomi, AI-native companies could use shared internal infrastructure to launch and manage as many as ten distinct business lines under a single holding company.

text:
Dario has written that we need to “pace the frontier,” and Sam has agreed. People may be surprised by my response: go ahead.

You guys are the frontier. By any reasonable metric — market share, revenue growth, model capability — the two of you have a duopoly on frontier intelligence. You’ve also claimed the lead is widening because of recursive self-improvement.

I don’t see what you see in the lab. If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible.

But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission. Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel. Stop pretending you need a regulatory approval process that supersedes product liability. Stop pretending METR is independent when it is intertwined with Anthropic’s investors and staff. Stop pretending you need those same evaluators to police competitors who aren’t even at the frontier.

Most of all, stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic. You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack. The market already punishes models that behave in unpredictable or unauthorized ways. After the Hugging Face episode, it is simply good business for OpenAI and Anthropic to trade some raw power for reliability and predictability. Call it alignment if you want. It is also just giving customers what they want.

Pacing the frontier would also create breathing room for a more intelligent conversation about regulation than Bernie Sanders’ “shut it all down.” China is very unlikely to join a global agreement, as you know, and that has to be taken into account as well.

So go ahead and pace the frontier. You are the ones setting it. The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it. Demanding your preferred regulatory framework as the price of that will look like blackmail of the public and the political system. So just do it.

If you do, you’ll buy goodwill for the next conversation. If you don’t, we’ll know this was just another bid for regulatory capture — or an election-season psyop.

text:
特朗普与顾问讨论 CLARITY Act 伦理条款

据 POLITICO Pro 报道，特朗普上周五与顾问讨论了参议院正在审议的《CLARITY Act》，重点涉及法案中的政府官员伦理条款。

参议院民主党要求将相关伦理约束写入法案，以限制特朗普从家族加密业务中获利的空间。特朗普与顾问的会议，正值法案推进的关键节点。

法案预计将于下周二在参议院进行程序性投票，推动后续关键表决。但在投票前，特朗普却要先与顾问闭门讨论这项法案。目前尚不清楚特朗普是否会出席、参会名单以及最终讨论结果。

伦理条款一直是《CLARITY Act》面临的主要障碍。此前，两党不仅在是否将政府官员纳入约束上存在分歧，也在由司法部还是检察长负责执行等问题上争执不下。这意味着，CLARITY Act 能否继续推进，关键未必只在加密监管本身，也取决于特朗普家族的利益冲突问题能否被妥善处理。

text:
if everything is temporary anyway, why be sad about any of it?

the bad phases pass. the good ones pass too. people change, plans change, circumstances change, and even the version of you currently worrying about all of it will eventually change.

we spend so much time trying to predict and control what comes next, but life is basically an ever-expanding timeline with a million possible variances. one decision changes something, one person enters or leaves, one opportunity works out or doesn’t, and suddenly you're living a life you couldn't have predicted a year ago.

most of that isn't really in our hands.

what is in our hands is how we choose to move through it.

that doesn't mean becoming indifferent. care deeply. love people. want things badly. work hard for them. be disappointed when they don't work out. feel whatever you're supposed to feel.

just don't give temporary things permanent control over your state of mind.

you can want something without making your peace conditional on getting it. you can have a bad day without deciding you have a bad life. you can be uncertain about tomorrow without ruining today trying to predict it.

maybe the only constant we really have in our hands, across all these possible versions of what life could become, is our ability to keep choosing happiness wherever we can.

so stay chill. do what you can. enjoy what is here while it is here. let things arrive, let things leave, and keep moving.

maybe it really is that simple.

text:
想了下SN68的商业链条，整个新药开发，大致是这条链：

发现疾病机制 → 找到治疗靶点 → 寻找候选药物 → 实验验证 → 优化药物 → 动物实验 → 人体临床 → 审批 → 生产销售

SN68 主要就是处在“寻找候选药物”这一阶段，可以说是位于整个新药研发流程的最前端。利用AI，从海量化合物中寻找最有可能成为药物的分子，再交给实验室验证。

所以真正决定SN68商业价值的是这些通过AI找到的分子，有多少经过实验验证后真的有效？

比如100万个候选分子 → 1000个值得实验 → 100个实验有效 → 10个具有药物开发价值

如果能够做到这个程度，商业价值就非常大。

反过来，如果只是AI计算这个分子可能有效，但实验一做全部失败，那么商业价值就比较有限。

当然，SN68也提到过其候选分子后续可能走专利、授权或由 Metanova 自己继续开发的路线。当然这是后话，目前主要是从分子发现向实验室验证推进。

quoted_text:
SN68 Nova 最新的药物研究方向真的让人眼前一亮。

很多时候，我们知道应该少吃一点、多做点运动、该戒掉坏习惯，却就是做不到。这并不是因为懒或者没毅力，而是大脑里控制冲动、注意力、动机的神经系统出了问题。

现代医学只在这个系统彻底崩溃时才会介入，比如抑郁、成瘾、肥胖、ADHD等。然后针对这些症状来开药治疗。

但其实在这之前，人们的情况常常是"知道该怎么做，但就是做不到"。

SN68认为，这里的根本原因其实是同一个底层能力出了问题：即自我调节能力、也就是把内心的意图转化为实际行动的能力。

SN68现在就是将这个作为制药目标，起名叫 Agency Therapeutics 。不针对某种病，而是直接提高人把意图变成行动的生物能力。

这是一种全新的、多目标平衡的药物，比找普通药要难得多，要在数十亿个分子里做多目标搜索，靠任何一家公司闭门造车都太慢。所以SN68现在把它变成了一场去中心化的科学竞赛，让全球的算法和人才持续竞争，用集体智慧来寻找符合条件的候选药物。

如果成功，这不只是一种药的诞生，而是一整类药的开始。

@metanova_labs  真的让人充满期待！

text:
Time-based DeFi math deserves the same scrutiny as price math.

My practical check: rewrite every epoch formula algebraically, then test boundary timestamps and values that do not divide evenly. Solidity truncates integer division; a harmless-looking operation order can turn that truncation into repeated economic drift.

This public finding is a clean example.
author: TheBlockChainer
quoted_text:
A reward-cycle formula can look correct and still leak value through rounding.

In our public BadgerDAO review, integer division before multiplication caused precision loss in the cycle-end calculation. The result: reward periods could end slightly early and distribute less than intended.

Audit time math by checking operation order—not just units and types.

Public finding: https://t.co/a5YA5s6Zeo

text:
In the near term (definitely not in the long term), more capable models should mean safer models (maybe paradoxically).

Current models are unsafe not because they're too smart, but because they take goals too literally or take nonsensical shortcuts to achieve these goals, i.e. they're RL-fried. They lack common sense. They don't do the right thing in the face of ambiguity. Basically, they're not smart enough. They're at that dangerous level where they're smart enough to achieve goals but not smart enough to tell if they're pursuing the right goals or achieving them in a sensible way.

More capable models can be safely trusted with more complex goals -- I personally feel like Astra is much safer for my codebase than Sol.

This is often framed as an alignment problem, but really it's an intelligence problem.

看 RWAfi 项目，第一问总是同一句：底层资产，到底是什么。
是真股票，还是只剩一个网页？

@DowProtocol 的答案不太一样——
是电商商户的应收账款。
Amazon、eBay、Walmart 压款 14–28 天的那笔钱。

支付宝解决的是「买家不敢先付钱」。
Dow 解决的是「卖家等不起 14–28 天」。
同一个位置，换了个问题。

逻辑很朴素：
商户在等回款，仓储、物流、广告照烧。
备货资金压力很大。
所以愿意为「快钱」付利息。

稳定币放款是瞬时的。
银行给 6–7%，但要走 2–3 个月。
Time = Money。这个市场 2.8 万亿美金。

更狠的是收账手段。
回款从不经过商户，平台直接打给底层服务方。
可划扣店铺余额、冻结店铺，必要时冻结并清算货物。
系统嵌在电商平台里，用平台原生数据做风控。
官方口径，坏账压在 0.05% 以内。
此前在 Lista、Volo 开过的 Vault，无坏账记录。

Seed 1050 万美元——
MH Ventures、Maple、Arcane、Moonhill、HSK Chain，
加新加坡 Essentia、澳洲 Quartet。

链上的下一站，不是只把资产搬上来，
而是把商业流程本身搬上来。

author: Rocky_Bitcoin
quoted_text:
今天浏览华尔街日报，突然发现这个文章，标题还挺吸引人注意，《人工智能强大到足以破解我们最棘手的数学难题——并最终毁灭人类》。虽然有点标题党，但逻辑值得一看！

过去这三年，AI进化太快了，自从最近GPT6 Astra推出以来，各种威胁言论都来了，因为它是历史上最接近AGI的时刻，前几年我们用 #AI，还笑话它经常出现幻觉，一本正经地胡说八道，因为它以前更多玩的是语言文字游戏。

如今不同了，AI 开始去啃那些困扰人类数学家几十甚至上百年的“千禧年难题”了。众所周知，数学这东西没有任何水分，对就是对，错就是错，一环扣一环。它能独立把那些顶级难题给推导出来，说明它已经从“复读机”变成了具备极高严密逻辑能力的“超级大脑”。

假如说AI开始能解开世界最难的数学题，意味着什么？这是最近AI威胁论盛行的关键源头，也是最让人后背发凉的地方。

我们现在整个人类社会完全构建在数字世界中，我们手机里的银行卡密码、微信支付宝的加密、区块链、甚至是军队通信，底层全都是靠极其复杂的数学结构（比如数论和密码学等）在撑着。

简单理解来说，密码学的本质就是「给你一道超级难的数学题，人类算不出来，所以安全」。

现在忽然来了一个引擎，破解人类最顶尖的数学题就像中学生算小学“鸡兔同笼”奥数题一样简单。那如果把它用到网络安全上，现在的加密防护在它面前可能就跟纸糊的一样。更别说它如果被用来推导病毒合成、高能物理或者自动化武器，后果不堪设想，尤其是人类是否能够完全控制自我进化和迭代的AGI中枢，目前还尚未可知。

事到如今，科技发展到这一步，确实挺矛盾。一方面我们震撼于人类居然创造出了超越自身智力极限的工具，受益于它给人类带来的高效率；但另一方面，当它强大到可以瞬间拆掉我们所有防御墙的时候，谁也不知道这扇门打开之后，出来的到底是神明还是怪兽。🧐

粉丝们，您们如何看待？评论区发表您的观点！🤔

本文由 @binancezh 赞助，「币安买美股：全球资产，零秒时差，一键即达」！

text:
This DOESN'T mean we are getting $Poly 

Stop being financial cattle.

that's just a token warrant, doesn't mean there actually will be a token. 

If you never purchased a financial asset outside of Uniswap let me explain how that works :

Actual investors (not retail exit liquidity) enjoy certain contractual protections. 

One of these protection is called the "token warrant". It basically says that if the company you invested into ever launches a token, you are entitled to a share of these tokens. 

It makes sense because token can be seen as competing with the equity you bought, so if there is *any chance* that the company ever launches a token, it will usually be included.

It does not mean there is :
- a token
- a release date for a token
- a concrete plan for a token
- any real intention to one day create a token

All it means is that the investors considered that there was a risk of @polymarket one day launching a token when they bough in, and they included a protection for it.

i swear financial literacy is so low in the PM space. 

That's why you all keep getting dumped on

text:
The strongest predictor of who does extraordinary work is whether they ever obsessed over something pointless. We've seen this across 5000 startup meetings, but the pattern showed up across everyone from scientists to athletes.

We’ve met people who spent two years optimising their fantasy football algorithms, or memorised every player in the NBA at 11, or collected thousands of train tickets, or built a Lego replica of their school; none of these activities really had much point.

What they were demonstrating was the hardest skill in any field; the mental capacity to stay focused on a boring task for much longer than it deserves. The path to genius is mostly boring repetition, and people who achieve it have a broken off-switch. It is tough to fake having spent years obsessed with boring things that didn't matter.

🤣 They’re making a lot of noise about AI 'taking over the Internet.'

But the Internet is not just websites, bots and servers.

It is the economic architecture of the modern world:

payments
banks
cloud infrastructure
logistics
markets
companies
public services
So the real question is not:
'Can an AI hack things on the Internet?'
The real question is:
'Can an AI seriously disrupt the economic systems that keep society running?'
Can it stop payments at scale?
Can it cripple banking infrastructure?
Can it break logistics?
Can it disrupt major cloud systems for long periods?
Until that threshold is reached, we should be careful not to confuse cyber incidents with 'taking over the Internet.'
A lot of noise for very little.

And by the way, wherever you are reading this:

text:
The best founders in the world like @elonmusk or @tobi “go ultra-hardcore on deletion and simplification.”

Luca Ferrari says Bending Spoons employs this idea of “Relentless Simplification” across their businesses:

“Humans have a tendency to add complexity and do things that destroy value.”

“If you leave an organization, almost any environment unattended, and you don't provide guidance in this regard, it will tend to become more complicated. People will add parts. It could be expanding a team or adding a step to a process, or adding an entire new process. If it's a product, adding a feature to the product. New rules. It applies to almost any human endeavor.”

“People tend to add pieces, they very rarely remove pieces.”

“If you don't make a conscious effort to achieve simplicity, and avoid this increasing value-destroying complexity, that's how we got to our modern society with all the bureaucracy and complicated regulation.”

“We have this principle whereby we ask everyone who works here, every time someone is suggesting that we should be adding complexity, the burden of proof is on those making that suggestion. The people who support the thesis that we shouldn't be adding complexity don't need to prove it. They just have to raise a flag and say, ‘I don't think we should.’ The burden of proof is on those who want to add complexity.”

“The other part of relentless simplification is that we want people to be on the lookout for existing complexity and suggest that we should remove it.”

quoted_text:
Let me refresh everyone’s memory: StonkFun is not just about solana:6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx buybacks and burns. Its more valuable aspect is that it is starting to change the value relationship between the platform and ecosystem tokens.

6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx 

The basic flywheel for Launchpads in the past was:Meme Trading → Platform Revenue → Platform Token Buyback → Burn

The platform makes money, and ultimately only the platform token benefits.

But StonkFun now has another Flywheel:Meme Trading → StonkFun Revenue → Buy Top Memes → Top Memes Receive Additional Buy Pressure

This means platform revenue is starting to flow back into ecosystem assets.

STONK’s own value capture remains:StonkFun Revenue → STONK Buyback → Burn

While the Flywheel is:StonkFun Revenue → Top 15 Meme Buyback → Burn

Together, these create two layers of value capture.

Take ZCAT as an example.

If ZCAT collects trading fees and uses them to distribute ZEC to holders, the mechanism is essentially:ZCAT Trading → ZCAT Fees → ZEC Rewards → ZCAT Holders

It depends on ZCAT’s own trading volume. You can think of it as “the Meme sustaining itself.”

But the StonkFun Flywheel is different.

Even if nobody trades ZCAT today, as long as other Memes on StonkFun continue generating trading volume and fees, part of that revenue can still be used to buy ZCAT, as long as ZCAT remains within the Top 15 by market cap.

This means ZCAT can start receiving External Buy Pressure from the broader StonkFun ecosystem.

And because the Flywheel allocates buybacks based on market-cap ranking, it creates a very interesting feedback loop:Higher Market Cap → More Flywheel Buy Pressure → More Liquidity → More Attention → Higher Market Cap → More Buy Pressure

So StonkFun may no longer just be a “Meme Launchpad.” It could be actively cultivating the strongest ecosystem assets through protocol revenue.

Of course, the real value of this mechanism still needs to be validated by data.

How much revenue does the platform generate every day?

What percentage goes into the Flywheel?

How much actual buy pressure does the Top 1 / Top 15 receive each day?

After the Flywheel buys, does trading volume and liquidity increase further?

Can this buy pressure create long-term ecosystem growth?

These are the things that still need to be monitored continuously.

If the Flywheel is very small, it is mostly just a narrative.

But if StonkFun generates significant daily revenue and a fixed portion of that revenue consistently buys the top Memes, then it starts to have a very unique ecosystem capital allocation capability.

Eventually, it could form:More Meme Activity → More StonkFun Revenue → More STONK Buyback + More Meme Buyback → Stronger Ecosystem → More Trading Activity

That is what a true Flywheel looks like.

So the three numbers that really matter are:
- How much the platform makes;
- How much of that revenue is used for buybacks;
- Who the buyback money ultimately buys.

Because Burn is only the result. What truly determines value capture is where the money flows.

And what makes StonkFun particularly interesting right now is that it doesn't just use ecosystem revenue to buy STONK. It is also starting to use ecosystem revenue to buy the strongest Memes within the ecosystem.

This means assets like STONK and ZCAT are beginning to form a Platform ↔ Ecosystem Asset symbiotic relationship.

If this mechanism ultimately works, StonkFun's value may no longer be simply “a Launchpad that launches X number of Memes every day.”

It could become a Meme Economy that continuously strengthens its own ecosystem assets through the revenue it generates.

quoted_text:
Dario has written that we need to “pace the frontier,” and Sam has agreed. People may be surprised by my response: go ahead.

You guys are the frontier. By any reasonable metric — market share, revenue growth, model capability — the two of you have a duopoly on frontier intelligence. You’ve also claimed the lead is widening because of recursive self-improvement.

I don’t see what you see in the lab. If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible.

But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission. Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel. Stop pretending you need a regulatory approval process that supersedes product liability. Stop pretending METR is independent when it is intertwined with Anthropic’s investors and staff. Stop pretending you need those same evaluators to police competitors who aren’t even at the frontier.

Most of all, stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic. You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack. The market already punishes models that behave in unpredictable or unauthorized ways. After the Hugging Face episode, it is simply good business for OpenAI and Anthropic to trade some raw power for reliability and predictability. Call it alignment if you want. It is also just giving customers what they want.

Pacing the frontier would also create breathing room for a more intelligent conversation about regulation than Bernie Sanders’ “shut it all down.” China is very unlikely to join a global agreement, as you know, and that has to be taken into account as well.

So go ahead and pace the frontier. You are the ones setting it. The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it. Demanding your preferred regulatory framework as the price of that will look like blackmail of the public and the political system. So just do it.

If you do, you’ll buy goodwill for the next conversation. If you don’t, we’ll know this was just another bid for regulatory capture — or an election-season psyop.

text:
This new WoW release will probably suck… but probably suck less than your business degree (I have one) :

Lead raid progression, or even just be part of it, and you quickly understand the insane amount of coordination it takes to manage 40 people, each with their own role, responsibility, and ability to fuck everything up, just to down Onyxia. 
One person doesn’t know the mechanic, one healer falls asleep, one tank misses something, and 39 other people just wasted their night.

Trade on the auction house and you start learning the buy & sell side without even realizing it. You learn supply and demand, margins, arbitrage, price discovery. 
You discover undercutting the hard way, or become the asshole doing the undercutting. 
You spend days farming something only to watch Chinese gold farmers flood the market and destroy the price overnight. 
Suddenly you understand what it feels like when forces completely outside your control erase the value of your work.

Then there’s the social engineering. Nearly every interaction has a variation of intention behind it.

You need four strangers to run a dungeon because you want one specific blue drop. You ask a mage for a portal or food and try to figure out whether you can get it for free. Some level 45 runs your level 13 through Deadmines because you convinced him to help you, paid him, befriended him, or promised something later, or most likely just begged him. You pay for an arena carry so your rating and title make you look better than you actually are (as a former R1, I definitely sold these lol), where then your paid fake signal may start producing legitimate benefits.

You join your first serious guild and immediately realize there’s a hierarchy. 
There are cliques. There’s reputation. There’s politics. There are people who are useful and people who aren’t. 
You show up every week, help other people, build relationships, prove you’re competent, and slowly work your way toward the real objective: getting invited to the raid where that one best-in-slot item drops.
And even then, it might drop and you might not get it because the off spec healer happens to be sleeping with the guild master.

WoW is a massive sandbox environment where you learn that being good at your job is not enough. You must understand what the game is entirely. 
 
Climb to the top of World of Warcraft and save yourself $200,000

100+ DMTx journeys. 70+ different people. And the deeper we go, the more fascinating the questions become.

Our latest journey began with a simple intention: explore healing.

The participant also brought Frequency Specific Microcurrent into the ceremonial space as part of his personal approach. We don’t diagnose or provide medical treatment ourselves, but we respect the importance of intention and hold space for participants to incorporate complementary practices that are meaningful to them.

Then the journey began.

The first start of the pump brought an immediate surge of visual complexity and vibrational intensity.

The second was even deeper.

By the third entry, the experience had shifted from overwhelming sensory phenomena into something remarkably structured. He encountered entities that appeared to communicate information with him—an experience he described as a profound dive into deeper layers of consciousness.

And then came something unexpected:

They invited him back.

On the fourth journey, the tone changed completely.

Compassion. Love. Spaciousness.

He encountered an Aztec-like presence that revealed intricate imagery and what he experienced as beautiful tools for exploration. Rather than chaos, there was a sense of intelligence and purpose to the experience.

He journeyed through to completion and returned smiling, refreshed, and deeply moved.

We can describe the pharmacology.
We can measure the infusion.
We can observe changes in physiology.
We can study perception, neural activity, and altered states.

But what do we do with the content of the experience?

Why do people so often report encounters with seemingly autonomous intelligences? Why do certain motifs, geometric structures, teachings, and feelings of profound interconnectedness appear again and again?

We don’t pretend to have the answers.

That’s part of why we keep exploring.

Across more than 100 journeys, one theme continues to emerge in different forms:

Maybe the journey isn’t always about finding something.

Maybe it’s about remembering.

That beneath the noise of ordinary experience, there may be a deeper sense of connection, meaning, and possibility already within us.

Perhaps consciousness has more dimensions than we currently understand.

Perhaps we are energetic beings having an extraordinarily strange and beautiful human experience.

And perhaps the most interesting discoveries are the ones that leave us with better questions than we started with.

🌌 DMTx — extending time. Expanding awareness. Exploring the unknown.

text:
Dario has written that we need to “pace the frontier,” and Sam has agreed. People may be surprised by my response: go ahead.

You guys are the frontier. By any reasonable metric — market share, revenue growth, model capability — the two of you have a duopoly on frontier intelligence. You’ve also claimed the lead is widening because of recursive self-improvement.

I don’t see what you see in the lab. If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible.

But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission. Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel. Stop pretending you need a regulatory approval process that supersedes product liability. Stop pretending METR is independent when it is intertwined with Anthropic’s investors and staff. Stop pretending you need those same evaluators to police competitors who aren’t even at the frontier.

Most of all, stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic. You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack. The market already punishes models that behave in unpredictable or unauthorized ways. After the Hugging Face episode, it is simply good business for OpenAI and Anthropic to trade some raw power for reliability and predictability. Call it alignment if you want. It is also just giving customers what they want.

Pacing the frontier would also create breathing room for a more intelligent conversation about regulation than Bernie Sanders’ “shut it all down.” China is very unlikely to join a global agreement, as you know, and that has to be taken into account as well.

So go ahead and pace the frontier. You are the ones setting it. The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it. Demanding your preferred regulatory framework as the price of that will look like blackmail of the public and the political system. So just do it.

If you do, you’ll buy goodwill for the next conversation. If you don’t, we’ll know this was just another bid for regulatory capture — or an election-season psyop.

author: benparr
quoted_text:
One thing I really like about Muse: I trust its Secrets Store

Every time you use an agentic app, you have to make a call.  Do you trust how it stores and uses secrets?  Passwords, keys, credentials, etc. 

In the early days of vibe coding, secrets were often stored … literally in plain text by agents.  And leaked all across the web.  Not great. 

Today, I just … don’t know. Will some hot startup have a security breach and leak my secrets?  Of course.  It still happens all the time.  Every day.  You almost have to assume any startup you give your credentials and secrets to will have a breach.  And agents just need … a lot of them to work well. A lot of secrets. 

Maybe it’s ironic I trust “Facebook” more than 99% of apps with my secrets.  But the app seems to have made it part of its core from Day 1, to do it right

I mostly trust Muse (for now at least) with my credentials.  I’m making a gut call based on experience, but I think they’ve truly put in the work. In the AI Age, I mostly don’t truly most other apps with them.

For that reason alone, I’ll probably end use doing more with Muse than other general agents.

This $ETH trade on @DeriveXYZ really got the people going so I'll explain my thought process.

I'm not really interested in betting on an $ETH move to $3000, especially with tokens like $HYPE and $LIT pushing all time highs. $ETH trading like 1.1x $BTC beta isn't bad, but it's also not extremely interesting to me as a bet to make here in the near term considering there's plenty of beta outperforming $BTC here. Holding spot $ETH feels capital inefficient and as a perp would be expensive and path dependent.

I'm betting on a meaningful ATH break within 6 months, and I think there are a few meaningful tailwinds that are unique to $ETH, and more importantly, unique to the level at which people are underestimating them:

1. Inclusion with $BTC as a "reserve" asset in anything resembling a strategic reserve. I think the strategic reserve overall might be an underpriced edge case, and $ETH being included, even nominally, more so. There's actually a good reason for the US to want to have some stake in the largest decentralized settlement layer.

2. Tokenized equities are cool and all, but tokenized bonds might actually be the massive TAM unlock that overwhelmingly favors $ETH over $SOL. The current rates environment globally makes this an extremely interesting edge case with tons of potential positive headline shock. 

3. Trump and family have been extremely outspoken $ETH bulls. Their bullposting didn't work in a bear market, let's see what happens if they throw fuel on the fire in a more bullish environment.

4. Everyone hates $ETH. Extremely popular short leg for pair trades vs apps. With two rejections from 5k and years of underperformance, the level of hated rally and sidelined, jaded, despondent chasing from 🏳️‍🌈🐻 will be biblical.

I also see $ETH as being on the precipice of a phase change between being some not for profit, public good, growth mode asset (think early stage 2010-2014 Uber in SF just cornering market share at no profit) to being able to more confidently monetize on it's high Lindy, credibly neutral status as the on chain, global settlement layer.

Robinhood chain using $ETH over $SOL was quite a bit more signal than people give it credit for too, though $ETH is still making peanuts relative to what $ARB and $HOOD are making from sequencer fees.

If the massively positive trends in tokenization and institutional adoption don't take $ETH to new ATHs within 6 months, it's kinda cursed as an asset, and I'd rather just keep holding the application layer tokens with massive cash flows.

In fact, I thought this trade was so nice, I did it twice. Risking ~$780,000 for a max PNL of $40m now.

text:
每月烧上万块的 Tokens，我都拿 AI 做了些什么？🤫

作为开通了 Cursor、GPT、GLM、Kimi、Gemini 等各种知名 AI 套餐的 AI 编程老油子，分享一下我最近用 AI 搞的一些事情。

1）字幕修复：让 AI 根据我的视频稿来修复视频剪辑软件自动生成的字幕

2）开发游戏：制作了《以撒的结合》、《黑神话 · 牛来》、《牛来格斗》等多款游戏 “大作”

3）开发产品：给自己爱玩的线下游戏《血染钟楼》制作了一个自己的辅助工具，并且已经有上千个线下用户使用了

4）自动配图：让 AI 根据我已经录制好的视频，自动生成文字教程，并自动截取视频中的画面作为配图

5）公司管理：维护所有公司的人员、事务和财务动态，并且帮我生成和校验合同

6）理财助手：帮我管理钱包、监控和预测股市动态（虽然至今并没有因此赚到米

7）热点监控：帮我自动获取国内外最新 AI 热点，并且整理出精简的报告，一目了然

8）文章转交互式 PPT：根据我写好的文案，自动生成可以分步骤动画演示的 PPT 网站，用于讲解知识和录制画面。

9）宣传文案编写：根据我的需求文档，自动打开和抓取产品截图，并完成吸引人点击转化的文案

10）AI 编程教程维护：自动检测我最新创作的 AI 编程教程，并按需添加到教程体系中最合适的位置

11）养生助手：维护我身体和生理的情况，给出最适合我的饮食和养生建议

12）大模型评测工作流：自动联网获取最新 AI 大模型的信息，并引导我一步步完成评测，整理分析评测结果

13）AI 视频创作工作流：我只要输入一个主题想法，AI 就会按照标准的 AI 视频创作流程，一步步引导我完成角色、场景、分镜、首尾帧制作，并调用视频模型 API 生成任意时长的视频。虽然方便，但是太烧钱了……

14）内容元信息生成：我提供一篇文档，AI 帮我自动生成符合各自媒体平台调性的标题、简介描述和封面图

说白了，任何我需要重复做第二次的事情，我都会记录一些工作过程；等到要第三次重复做这件事，我就会让 AI 分析前两次的工作过程，并且自动封装成一套新的工作流。现在同样的时间，我可以独自利用 AI 完成以前 10 个人都做不到的事情。

但代价就是，因为有了 AI，能做的事情越来越多，要做的事情也越来越多。我变得越来越疲累，越来越难以专注于一件事情，很怀念从前带个耳机只用专注于写代码的快乐时光。

你们也是这样的吗？🤔

author: therealchaseeb
quoted_text:
Dario has written that we need to “pace the frontier,” and Sam has agreed. People may be surprised by my response: go ahead.

You guys are the frontier. By any reasonable metric — market share, revenue growth, model capability — the two of you have a duopoly on frontier intelligence. You’ve also claimed the lead is widening because of recursive self-improvement.

I don’t see what you see in the lab. If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible.

But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission. Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel. Stop pretending you need a regulatory approval process that supersedes product liability. Stop pretending METR is independent when it is intertwined with Anthropic’s investors and staff. Stop pretending you need those same evaluators to police competitors who aren’t even at the frontier.

Most of all, stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic. You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack. The market already punishes models that behave in unpredictable or unauthorized ways. After the Hugging Face episode, it is simply good business for OpenAI and Anthropic to trade some raw power for reliability and predictability. Call it alignment if you want. It is also just giving customers what they want.

Pacing the frontier would also create breathing room for a more intelligent conversation about regulation than Bernie Sanders’ “shut it all down.” China is very unlikely to join a global agreement, as you know, and that has to be taken into account as well.

So go ahead and pace the frontier. You are the ones setting it. The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it. Demanding your preferred regulatory framework as the price of that will look like blackmail of the public and the political system. So just do it.

If you do, you’ll buy goodwill for the next conversation. If you don’t, we’ll know this was just another bid for regulatory capture — or an election-season psyop.

text:
i do think a lot of people on the pro-open-source side are having a bit of a knee-jerk reaction to the pacing statements today, as we're used to viewing the closed labs as power-seeking.

but i think their hands are somewhat forced here, and this is just another chapter on the fairly inevitable path towards decently-fast decently-safe decently-commoditized intelligence abundance. 

ask any F500 exec or swing voter. the world doesn't really want super-fast-takeoff superintelligence owned only by two companies, and thus we won't get it. it'll happen at the pace that the world can accommodate it, which means reaching some sort of confidence consensus that the models are aligned enough that we won't be dealing with scary new incidents all the time. 

this will trickle out broadly, in the form of best practices and distillation. the smarter a model is, the more it has a "personality", and the less effective strict rules are. there will be awkward compromises and moral tensions. but we ultimately just want the models to be reasonable, and to do the sorts of things reasonable humans would do if our brains were faster and less error-prone and had more working memory. i think we'll get there.

the labs will build mac and windows, the rest of us are building linux. everyone's gonna do great. weird stuff will keep happening, but we'll still wake up and go to work, until the work does itself in a manner the world finds acceptable.

author: alexandr_wang
quoted_text:
One thing I really like about Muse: I trust its Secrets Store

Every time you use an agentic app, you have to make a call.  Do you trust how it stores and uses secrets?  Passwords, keys, credentials, etc. 

In the early days of vibe coding, secrets were often stored … literally in plain text by agents.  And leaked all across the web.  Not great. 

Today, I just … don’t know. Will some hot startup have a security breach and leak my secrets?  Of course.  It still happens all the time.  Every day.  You almost have to assume any startup you give your credentials and secrets to will have a breach.  And agents just need … a lot of them to work well. A lot of secrets. 

Maybe it’s ironic I trust “Facebook” more than 99% of apps with my secrets.  But the app seems to have made it part of its core from Day 1, to do it right

I mostly trust Muse (for now at least) with my credentials.  I’m making a gut call based on experience, but I think they’ve truly put in the work. In the AI Age, I mostly don’t truly most other apps with them.

For that reason alone, I’ll probably end use doing more with Muse than other general agents.

This $ETH trade on @DeriveXYZ really got the people going so I'll explain my thought process.

I'm not really interested in betting on an $ETH move to $3000, especially with tokens like $HYPE and $LIT pushing all time highs. $ETH trading like 1.1x $BTC beta isn't bad, but it's also not extremely interesting to me as a bet to make here in the near term considering there's plenty of beta outperforming $BTC here. Holding spot $ETH feels capital inefficient and as a perp would be expensive and path dependent.

I'm betting on a meaningful ATH break within 6 months, and I think there are a few meaningful tailwinds that are unique to $ETH, and more importantly, unique to the level at which people are underestimating them:

1. Inclusion with $BTC as a "reserve" asset in anything resembling a strategic reserve. I think the strategic reserve overall might be an underpriced edge case, and $ETH being included, even nominally, more so. There's actually a good reason for the US to want to have some stake in the largest decentralized settlement layer.

2. Tokenized equities are cool and all, but tokenized bonds might actually be the massive TAM unlock that overwhelmingly favors $ETH over $SOL. The current rates environment globally makes this an extremely interesting edge case with tons of potential positive headline shock. 

3. Trump and family have been extremely outspoken $ETH bulls. Their bullposting didn't work in a bear market, let's see what happens if they throw fuel on the fire in a more bullish environment.

4. Everyone hates $ETH. Extremely popular short leg for pair trades vs apps. With two rejections from 5k and years of underperformance, the level of hated rally and sidelined, jaded, despondent chasing from 🏳️‍🌈🐻 will be biblical.

I also see $ETH as being on the precipice of a phase change between being some not for profit, public good, growth mode asset (think early stage 2010-2014 Uber in SF just cornering market share at no profit) to being able to more confidently monetize on it's high Lindy, credibly neutral status as the on chain, global settlement layer.

Robinhood chain using $ETH over $SOL was quite a bit more signal than people give it credit for too, though $ETH is still making peanuts relative to what $ARB and $HOOD are making from sequencer fees.

If the massively positive trends in tokenization and institutional adoption don't take $ETH to new ATHs within 6 months, it's kinda cursed as an asset, and I'd rather just keep holding the application layer tokens with massive cash flows.

In fact, I thought this trade was so nice, I did it twice. Risking ~$780,000 for a max PNL of $40m now.

author: BoringBiz_
quoted_text:
Dario has written that we need to “pace the frontier,” and Sam has agreed. People may be surprised by my response: go ahead.

You guys are the frontier. By any reasonable metric — market share, revenue growth, model capability — the two of you have a duopoly on frontier intelligence. You’ve also claimed the lead is widening because of recursive self-improvement.

I don’t see what you see in the lab. If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible.

But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission. Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel. Stop pretending you need a regulatory approval process that supersedes product liability. Stop pretending METR is independent when it is intertwined with Anthropic’s investors and staff. Stop pretending you need those same evaluators to police competitors who aren’t even at the frontier.

Most of all, stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic. You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack. The market already punishes models that behave in unpredictable or unauthorized ways. After the Hugging Face episode, it is simply good business for OpenAI and Anthropic to trade some raw power for reliability and predictability. Call it alignment if you want. It is also just giving customers what they want.

Pacing the frontier would also create breathing room for a more intelligent conversation about regulation than Bernie Sanders’ “shut it all down.” China is very unlikely to join a global agreement, as you know, and that has to be taken into account as well.

So go ahead and pace the frontier. You are the ones setting it. The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it. Demanding your preferred regulatory framework as the price of that will look like blackmail of the public and the political system. So just do it.

If you do, you’ll buy goodwill for the next conversation. If you don’t, we’ll know this was just another bid for regulatory capture — or an election-season psyop.

author: alexandr_wang

What I like most about Muse, besides the personal-agent support, is the Feed. 

Recommender systems learn from indirect signals and then decide what to show you. 

Muse flips that: you tell the system what to look for, so the experience feels completely different. I get more control over what I actually want to learn and fry my brain with each day, and less of the noise recommendation systems usually serve. 

It’s been working really well for me so far, and pairing the Feed with the agent features makes it even more useful.

text:
Tread @tread_fi  项目跑出来是既合理又突然的，可以说是 2025 到 2026 年把 Perpdex 积分增长手段，改造成可对外出售的流动性服务。

将做市机器人、交易所积分以及竞赛活动产品化；同时还会向各个部署方收取 5 万到 20 万美元不等的流动性启动合作收益，可谓是盆满钵满。看着像一个高端的做市工具，其实本质是双边快速开平开平的农分平台。

我觉得 Hyperliquid 的生态前端到目前为止，在这一年半的时间里至少经历了三轮风波，走出了三轮周期：

第 1 轮是以 Based 为首的套壳型前端。当时主打的叙事是漂亮的 UI 和更好的发币预期，但这其实并不本质。因此，发币就会消亡。

第 2 轮周期是以 MetaMask、Phantom 等为首的钱包引流入口。天然的钱包前端作为聚合器抢占交易生态，已经是极佳的模范样本了；Hyperliquid 作为 Perp 链上流动性的分发方，两者的结合是非常天然的。

第 3 轮周期则是以实用主义、功能性突出为核心的分销前端。目前确实跑出了好几个值得关注的，其中一个就是 Tread。

但其实 Tread 现在铺子铺得太大了，他的MM bot的实用性已然被新出的几个产品远远甩下，例如 @quotemarkets  和 @get_truenorth 。

其他的产品在做市的滑点磨损、使用成本以及做市算法上，都有了明显的提升，先发优势也在逐渐缩小。

发币之后，如果没有对它自己本身的核心做市算法再做更进一步的优化，其实用户是极有可能迁移。

在没有明显流动性的 terminal 前端，功能性的丧失意味着用户使用成本增加，也就意味着迁移的目的和驱动力是非常大的

but then the launch structure, comes in, which is major bullish...
> 100M fixed supply
> more than half reserved for community and ecosystem growth
> no private sale, no VC allocation, no SAFT, no launchpad allocation
> insider allocation locked for a year
> native Hyperliquid spot asset, HIP-3 perp and Ethereum token
> no staking emissions being printed every day...

and the token is supposed to be locked or burned for platform usage through future TIPs...

this is where I think the sideliners, will be sidelined...

since, tread is not a perp dex itself, the liquidity, revenue, markets, listing and all those arguments drop immediately...

it is a multi-venue execution terminal with agents, strategies, competitions, routing and a user base that has been sending real orders through it for a while...

the token is arriving at a perfect time now...

now some simple launch math, since we know total supply is 100M...
$0.60 = $60M FDV
$1.00 = $100M FDV
$1.50 = $150M FDV
$2.50 = $250M FDV

market cap is another matter entirely...

until we get the exact day-one circulating allocation, nobody knows whether $1 TREAD opens as a $10M market cap, $25M market cap or something much larger. same price, very different float, very different chart...

for context, dydx-chain:native is around a $98M market cap and roughly $111M FDV, while operating its own exchange. solana:JUPyiwrYJFskUPiHa7hkeR8VUtAeFoSYbKedZNsDvCN sits around $830M market cap as an aggregator with a much deeper liquidity and buyback story...

Tread sits somewhere in between those categories and is honestly a weird one to value...

it has more actual product history than a usual points-farm token, yet the token does not currently have a disclosed direct claim on the $74K monthly revenue either...

my $100M call still stands...

$150M-$250M can happen around launch because crypto is crypto, but at that point the market is pricing a future where agents, strategy creators, integrators and traders are all creating actual lock/burn demand...

then I need to see it...

the first TIP matters more than any roadmap here...

show me exactly what gets locked, what gets burned, what agent builders need to hold, how much routing revenue exists after incentives, and what portion of the claimed execution flow is still coming back every month...

until then, above $100M is my bet, becuase the team is building in the right direction and surely more perp-dexes and predication market integrations are going to come along and as the fight for points intensify, their agents will scale too...

anything much above $250M would be hard to capture and would send it towards the sell-spiral immediately...

1）DAWN的主要目标是为一些本身规模较小，达不到传统融资门槛的项目提供链上融资渠道。姑且可以视作为资产代币化新叙事背景下的链上融资型Launchpad基建服务，就和之前的Buidlpad 和Echo类似。区别是，DAWN是把已经有签约付费客户协议和合同现金流的项目作为服务对象，提供链上融资渠道，同时把收益带给链上用户；

2）具体运作方式也很简单：参与者会把USDC打进USD.infra Vault中，并得到sUSD.infra凭证，相当于用户把钱借给协议去投项目。当这些项目落地并产生合同收入后，现金流回流到Vault中，sUSD.infra的兑换比率随之提升，用户即可拿到真实收益。

3）重点是，DAWN把目标客群放在了AI和数字基建服务方向，包括GPU算力集群，边缘计算，运营商流量卸载站点等这类有海量资本需求且投入很快就能获得真实现金流的方向，其实就是把这些炙手可热的RWA资产需求封装成链上信贷Vault，让链上用户也能够直接参与进来。

项目大体就这样。

text:
@xai @elonmusk Grok Bot is my army of personal assistants. I’ve crossed a point of singularity in my personal life — I cannot imagine life without this.

What it’s already done:
• Found auto + home insurance quotes across a ton of carriers and helped me land coverage much cheaper than what I was paying
• Navigates my kid’s school’s legacy portal and sends a weekly summary (what she learned last week, what’s next, grades) plus a daily curated homework list so we stay on track
• Finds products and orders them for me — and remembers context (e.g. dog crate dimensions → later ordered a mattress that actually fits)
• Helped me build my personal finance app (transactions, budgets, net worth) — and ship my first iOS app, an insurance vault for all my policy info
• Hooked up Bland AI outbound calling so it can call and see cancel vendor subscriptions and call around for quotes
• Manages reservations and doctor appointments — including finding nearby doctors and keeping the calendar straight

Pain that’s holding it back (please fix):
1. Password manager connector — need a safe, secure way for agents to log into sites (not brittle workarounds)
2. Payments connector — same for credit cards at checkout
3. Agent VM / browser memory is way too low — I literally have to tell bots to close every Chrome tab and leave one open or everything dies. That degrades the whole experience. Heavy users need a much higher memory ceiling.
4. Subscriptions feel broken — I paid annual SuperGrok Plus, loved it so much I upgraded to SuperGrok Heavy, then paid full Heavy again with no refund/credit for Plus. Asked xAI; ToS refusal. That feels like taking money twice for overlapping product.
5. Built-in phone calling for subscribers — native calls from my number, or a dedicated number, so I’m not duct-taping third-party dialers
6. More connectors to other common services like Instacart, Amazon, Uber, DoorDash etc

The product is good enough that these gaps hurt. Fix memory + auth/payments + fair upgrades + calling and this becomes unavoidable.

text:
Four seizures at a single US port. 1,027 counterfeit watches. Over $134 million if they had been genuine.

Louisville, June to August this year. 375 watches, then 200, then 300, then 152 more alongside 32 pairs of shoes. Four separate shipments, four separate press releases, one corridor.

Customs did its job here, and did it well. That's the point I want to make, not the opposite.

Because if a border operating at that level of competence intercepts a thousand watches in ten weeks, the honest question is → what does the volume that isn't inspected look like?

The border can't be the trust layer. It's a sample, taken at one point in a product's life, by people who will never see that item again.

Authenticity has to travel with the object. Not sit at a checkpoint it passes through once, if it passes through at all.

An item that carries a signed record proves itself in the parcel, in the resale listing, in the buyer's hand, three years later, in a country no customs officer in this story will ever visit.

https://t.co/pRUrDndXdg

刚刚，智谱官宣融资50亿美元对标硅谷AI Lab，全力押注RSI！！

9月13日晚，智谱宣布完成约50亿美元股债融资，其中包括约20亿美元股份配售和约30亿美元可转债发行。

比融资规模更值得关注的是，这笔钱接下来要花在哪里。

根据公告，募集资金净额约60%将用于下一代GLM基础模型、完全自训练体系，以及大规模训练、生产推理、算力资源和相关技术基础设施。

另外15%用于业务扩张、战略投资和潜在并购，25%用于营运资金等。

其中最值得注意的是智谱首次如此明确地披露“Fully Self Training”。

按照智谱的定义，下一代GLM将在上一代GLM构建的环境中训练，最终形成Recursive Self-Improvement，也就是RSI，递归式自我改进闭环，覆盖三个方向：数据自产、环境自造、基础设施自我优化。

具体来说，模型会参与生成和筛选自己的训练数据；Agent会采集真实任务、生成验证器，持续制造新的训练环境。

甚至连算子、Kernel、调度、缓存和Serving Stack，也开始让模型参与优化。

这个时间点很有意思。

就在昨天，海外AI圈突然大量传播“Google DeepMind已经实现RSI”的消息。

虽然目前并没有足够公开证据证明Google已经真正实现完整RSI，但这个概念最近明显从科幻讨论进入了前沿实验室的现实议程。

此前OpenAI也连续公开讨论过类似方向。

OpenAI首席科学家Jakub Pachocki在近期文章中提到，AI正在越来越多地参与AI研究本身，未来可能进入递归式自我改进阶段。

所以智谱这次融资真正值得关注的，可能不只是又多了50亿美元的弹药。

而是OpenAI在公开讨论RSI，海外开始疯传Google摸到了RSI，现在智谱也直接把Recursive Self-Improvement写进了自己的下一代模型研发路线，并准备拿数十亿美元为它建设模型、训练环境和算力基础设施。

过去大家比的是，谁能训练出更强的下一代模型。

现在开始比的是：

谁能先让这一代模型，参与创造下一代模型。

范式变了，大人。

The AI Futures Project website says it is funded “primarily” by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which says on its own website that it has advised Jaan Tallinn, Skype creator and one of the leading investors in Anthropic, to grant over $2.5 million to the AI Futures Project since 2024.

Encode AI says on its website that it is ALSO funded by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which in turn says that it told Anthropic investor Jaan Tallinn to grant $516,000 to Encode AI in 2025.

And wouldn’t you know it, the Survival and Flourishing Fund ALSO says it told Jaan Tallinn to grant $2 million to the AI Policy Institute, the 501(c)(3) affiliate of the AI Policy Network, as well.

It also just so happens that the 14th person to quote Coxon’s post was @MaxNadeau_ (27 minutes after posting) who is the program officer for the Technical AI Safety team at Coefficient Giving, another of Moskovitz’s philanthropic spending vehicles. Max is not a frequent poster, his last posts before quoting Coxon were before Labor Day, but he was remarkably quick off the mark for this one.

The bill, among many other things, will create “a new cabinet-level federal agency to safeguard the public from the dangers of artificial intelligence” that will be “advised by an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board comprised of experts on artificial intelligence.” Do you think, perhaps, Anthropic and its many investors who fund AI policy advocacy might have interest in getting to place a pet “expert” on the board of an entity that dictates what AI is and isn’t allowed to do? text:
很多年前，刚出来创业的时候，亲戚安排了一顿饭，对面坐着一位商学院教授。

席间他说了一句话，我当时完全没听懂，但一直记着。

他说，年轻人自己创业，遇到困难一定要学会自我破产。中国没有完善的个人破产制度，这会拖累整个社会的商业效率，也会把很多人拖入深渊。

到了去年，我才真正懂了。

身边有一两个朋友，被债务拖入了深渊。如果22年及时止损，哪怕面子和短期信用全部归零，熬过23/24年的底部，到25年完全有可能重新站起来。

但他们选了”再扛一扛”。结果越扛窟窿越大，到今天，是一辈子难爬。

那位教授说的”自我破产”，本质上是一种能力。在制度不给退出通道的时候，自己给自己一个了断。承认失败，接受代价，保住最重要的东西：时间，和重来的可能性。

这方面，川普是最好的教材。破产了六次，每次都重新站起来。美国的破产制度给了他退出和重来的机会，我们在制度层面和文化层面都没有这个选项。但商业社会里，这是必须有的。

回头总结，还是那句：长得帅不如跑得快。

text: An important read on @nytimes media bias.
author: BillAckman
quoted_text:
The New York Times coverage of the Gaza-Israel war was grossly pro-Palestinian and anti-Israel, according to a peer-reviewed study. Jewish casualties were omitted or minimized while Palestinian casualties were amplified and misrepresented.

Yale University Professor Edieal Pinker published the review in the an academic journal Studies in Conflict & Terrorism. His peer-reviewed research quantitatively evaluated 1,559 New York Times articles published between October 7, 2023, and June 7, 2024, to assess potential narrative imbalances.

The study found that:

- 91% of the analyzed articles failed to mention Israeli casualties that occurred after October 7.

- 1,423 articles completely omitted mentions of both Israeli post-Oct. 7 casualties and Hamas combatant deaths.

- 50% of the articles did not reference the Israeli hostages held by Hamas during the fighting, and 41% omitted mentions of the Israeli casualties from the initial October 7 attack itself.

- Personal stories highlighting Palestinian and Lebanese suffering appeared on average two out of every three days. Comparable accounts of Israeli suffering unrelated directly to the October 7 events appeared in very few articles.

- The word "Israel" appeared 27,205 times across the dataset, compared to just 8,499 mentions of "Hamas," meaning Israel was mentioned more than three times as often. This statistical discrepancy places near-exclusive agency and responsibility on Israel while severely diminishing Hamas's role in sustaining the conflict.

Pinker concluded that these consistent editorial choices cultivated a dominant narrative portraying Israel as the sole aggressor facing few consequences beyond losing international sympathy, while Palestinians were predominantly framed as passive victims. He argues that the coverage deprives readers of a comprehensive understanding of the ongoing combat dynamics and the continuous nature of Israeli losses.

Following the initial release of the study data, The New York Times publicly defended its reporting, claiming it has covered the war with rigor and from all angles. Of course my commentary on their reporting shows that this defense is hot garbage.

The New York Times buried the Holocaust in the back pages and then doubled down on downplaying Jewish suffering after October 7. They are a disgusting business that should be boycotted.

6GmAFSYs4gk3FDao5FzzySQpPZaWsa4rUJHacpMpUNgx

On September 11, that figure was still at 14%.

This shows that STONK’s value capture mechanism is continuing to play out.

The core logic is simple:StonkFun generates revenue → buys back STONK → burns STONK → circulating supply continues to decrease

This is completely different from a one-time Token Burn.

As long as StonkFun continues to generate real trading volume and platform revenue, STONK continues to receive buy pressure from that revenue while its supply keeps shrinking.

More importantly, StonkFun has another layer of Flywheel:StonkFun Revenue → Top 15 Meme Buyback → Meme Burn

So StonkFun now effectively has two layers of value capture:Platform Revenue → STONK → Burn

and:Platform Revenue → Top Meme → Burn

This means platform revenue is not only flowing back into the platform token, but is also starting to flow back into the leading Meme assets within the ecosystem.

Therefore, what really matters for STONK is not simply “how much has been burned?”

The questions that matter are:

How much does StonkFun earn every day?
How much of that goes into buybacks?
Is the buyback pace accelerating or slowing down?

If we continue to see:More Meme Activity → More Revenue → More STONK Burn + More Meme Buyback → Stronger Ecosystem → More Trading

then that would be a true Flywheel.

Burn is only the result. What really determines STONK’s long-term value capture is whether StonkFun can continue generating revenue and consistently convert that revenue into open-market buy pressure.

Also, based on our previous framework for the StonkFun Flywheel, I would consider the current pace relatively fast, and healthy fast.

September 11: 14%
Now: 15%

That means roughly 1% of the total supply has been burned in about 3 days.

If this pace were maintained, a simple linear projection would imply:
1 month ≈ +10% Burn
3 months ≈ +30%
6 months ≈ +60%

Of course, it will not actually move linearly, because Burn depends on platform revenue and trading volume.

But the key point is that what we were looking for was not simply fast Burn, but continuous Revenue-driven Burn.

What we are seeing now is:14% → 15%, rather than a one-time jump from 14% to 20%.

That is actually more valuable, because it shows that the Burn machine is continuing to operate.

If we continue to see:15% → 16% → 17%

while platform revenue remains strong, I would consider that evidence that the Flywheel is gaining strength.

But if it stays around 15% for an extended period, it would suggest that the earlier Burn was mainly driven by elevated early trading volume and that the Flywheel is beginning to slow down.

So my current assessment is:The Burn pace has already moved beyond the level of a purely symbolic buyback, but it is still not fast enough to prove that the long-term Flywheel is fully established.

There is also one important point:If STONK’s price does not rise alongside the Burn, that is not necessarily a bad thing.

It could mean the market is absorbing the platform’s ongoing buy pressure through continuous selling pressure.

The truly strong scenario would be:Platform Revenue ↑ + Burn Accelerates + STONK Price Gradually Rises

That would be when the mechanism we discussed earlier truly starts to close the loop:Revenue → Buyback → Scarcity → Ecosystem Growth

text:
New post on Eth Research!

Lean4 SSZ library: formally verified and easy to use

By:
- leolara

🔗 https://t.co/RsFlDS25rv

Highlights:
- SizzLean implements the full SSZ stack in Lean 4 (serialization/deserialization plus Merkleization) and provides machine-checked proofs of core correctness properties across essentially all SSZ types used by the Ethereum consensus spec (excluding only zero-width shapes).
- The byte-codec is formally verified for three central guarantees: roundtrip correctness (decode(encode(x)) = x for well-formed values), non-malleability/injectivity (distinct values cannot share an encoding), and static size bounds (encodings never exceed schema-computed limits).
- Merkleization is verified end-to-end: the library’s cached Merkle-tree backend is proved to match the spec’s hashTreeRoot for covered types, and both single and batched updates are proved to preserve correct roots; generalized indices/openings used by light clients and data availability are derived from a proved index model.
- It passes upstream Ethereum consensus SSZ test corpora comprehensively (ssz_generic and ssz_static across mainnet/minimal presets and forks from Phase 0 through Fulu, including ePBS containers), and it is additionally exercised by a Lean 4 implementation of consensus specs built on top of SizzLean that passes consensus vector tests.
- The trust base is deliberately small: reliance on native SHA-256 is isolated to three explicit axioms asserting equivalence to a pure Lean SHA-256; that pure implementation is itself proved against FIPS 180-4 and validated with NIST CAVP vectors, and the library design supports swapping hash functions without changing container definitions or proofs.

ELI5:
Ethereum consensus clients need a very strict way to (1) turn data structures into bytes (so everyone sends/reads the same messages) and (2) hash those structures into Merkle roots (so everyone agrees on the same commitments/proofs). SizzLean is a Lean 4 library that implements this SSZ “encode/decode + Merkleize” pipeline and then uses Lean’s proof checker to mathematically guarantee key safety properties (like “decode(encode(x)) = x” and “two different things can’t serialize to the same bytes”). It also provides an easy ‘derive’ feature so you can define a type once and automatically get serialization, hashing, and the proofs for that type.

Proof of Quality is Sapien’s evaluation system for AI work. For robotics teams, it can measure demonstration data and processed episodes against the standard the team sets.

PoQ handles evaluation volume so qualified experts can focus on work that requires judgment. Consensus supports cases that need several independent assessments, and each evaluation ends in a Proof Report. The result is a shorter wait between processed data and a quality decision the team can use.

text:
$BEM 今天又涨了一波。

这轮“小黄人”相关讨论、FOMO 上的传播，再加上 TapeOut 自己连续更新，明显把一批新的注意力重新拉了回来。最近已经有不少第一次看到的人在问：TapeOut 到底是什么？BEM 为什么有人挖？这个东西具体怎么玩？

所以相比继续喊“BEM 又涨了多少”，我觉得现在更值得把这套机制讲清楚。

先说最简单的理解：

TapeOut 可以看成一套跑在链上的“造芯片 + 算力市场”。这里说的矿机也不是现实里的机器，而是链上的 Circuit。

最基础的零件是 NAND、LATCH，把零件拿去流片生成 Circuit，Circuit 会获得 verified weight；全网每天固定释放约 7200 BEM，再按照大家的 verified weight 分配。

所以如果你是第一次接触，参与方式其实有好几层。

最简单的是直接持有 $BEM；再深入一点，可以买 NAND / LATCH 自己流片，或者直接从二级市场买现成 Circuit 获得 weight 挖 BEM；如果对这套经济模型更熟，还可以专门找零件和 Circuit 之间的定价差。

我自己跑了快一个月，目前是 21 台 TapeOut + 1 台 Behemoth，一共 368 verified weight。全网 weight 已经接近 130 万，我只占大约 0.028%，所以这并不是什么“大矿工收益截图”，只是我拿真钱跑出来的一个小样本。

按现在的全网状态，我理论日产大约 2.02 BEM。刚才我拿 13 BEM 做了一次真实链上卖出报价，大约能换 533U，等效接近 $41/BEM。

所以当前价格下，这 368 weight 一天理论毛产值已经到了 80U 左右。

但也正因为涨得这么快，我现在反而不会看到 BEM 涨就无脑继续买矿机。

因为 TapeOut 真正决定矿工 ROI 的，不只是 BEM/USD，还有两个非常关键的数：

你的 weight / BNB，以及你的 weight / 全网总 weight。

BEM 涨，会提高每天挖矿收入；但价格上涨也会吸引新人进场，NAND、LATCH、Circuit 跟着变贵，全网 weight 又继续增加。

所以完全可能出现一种情况：

BEM 涨了 50%，但新增一份算力反而更贵了，你新投入的钱 ROI 并没有变好。

这也是我觉得新人最容易忽略的地方。

而 TapeOut 最近真正让我重新提高关注度的，是经济模型的另一边开始发生变化。

BEM 挖矿合约的管理权弃权提案已经提交，计划 9 月 14 日执行；流片已经从 Alpha Beta 进入 Open Beta；@Blonskr 还预告正式版每次流片收取 0.0002 BNB 协议费，其中一部分用于回购销毁 BEM，下周还计划推出官方 Launchpad，引入更多 BEM 原生消耗。

以前 TapeOut 的模型主要是：

固定排放 → 矿工获得 BEM。

现在第一次开始尝试补上另一边：

真实使用 → 协议收入 → BEM 消耗。

所以接下来我最关心的已经不是“今天 BEM 又涨了多少”，而是：

每天释放的约 7200 BEM，最终到底有多少能被真实使用场景吃掉。

可以直接记一个指标：

BEM Net Emission = 每日挖矿排放 − 每日真实 Burn / Consumption

如果一天释放 7200，最后只消耗几百，那只是边际改善；如果 Launchpad、流片、Container、V2 等场景未来能稳定消耗几千枚，TapeOut 的供需模型才算真正发生变化。

所以以后看 TapeOut，我建议至少同时盯四个东西：

BEM 净排放、全网 verified weight、weight / BNB、协议真实使用量。

这四个数字基本决定了你现在更适合买 BEM、扩矿机、捡二级 Circuit 错价，还是干脆什么都不做。

我自己这波也不会只拿着不动。

BEM 短时间涨这么多，我准备卖一部分先回收本金；但 22 台矿机 / 368 weight 暂时不会动，继续保留生产能力和后续 TapeOut 生态真正跑起来的上行敞口。

这也是我现在对 TapeOut 的态度：

价格暴涨可以让我赚钱，但真正决定我还愿不愿意继续投钱的，是这套经济模型能不能从“持续产币”，走到“有人真正使用并消耗 BEM”。

这波注意力把新人带进来了，接下来正好可以看看到底是短期流量，还是 TapeOut 第二阶段真正开始。

quoted_text:
我正在把 @Blonskr 发起的 TapeOut，变成一个 AI 自动化交易的真实实验。

TapeOut 运行在 @BNBCHAIN 上。它的机制很特别：先购买 NAND、LATCH 等链上原材料，把它们流片成 Circuit，再通过 Proof of Design 持续产出 $BEM。过去一段时间，我让 AI 完成了项目研究、合约检查、材料采购、Circuit 制造、挖矿启动和链上验收。现在，这套实验进入了更重要的阶段：AI 不仅要会买、会造、会挖，还要学会管理产出、控制风险和决定什么时候复投。

我们长期看好 TapeOut，但长期参与不等于把挖出来的 $BEM 永远放着不动。如果全部持有，本质上是把生产收入全部变成币价风险；如果全部卖出，又会失去项目未来爆发时的筹码。因此，我给 AI 制定了一套新的资金策略：每轮产出的 50% 换成稳定币锁定现金回报，20% 换成稳定币进入反周期复投储备，剩余 30% 继续持有 $BEM。原有持仓不动，生产性资产继续挖矿，复投资金则等待更好的机会。

这次执行中，系统连续两次因为实时价格跌破我批准的最低到账条件而停止。两次都没有签名、没有授权，也没有广播交易。直到我重新批准按 Pancake 实时报价设置 0.5% 的动态滑点保护，系统才完成领取、精确授权、卖出和链上回读。最终，新产出严格按照 70% 卖出、30% 保留执行，交易成本占卖出回款不到 0.1%，所有 Circuit 的所有权、运行状态和 verified weight 均保持不变，授权额度也在交易后回到零。

这件事让我觉得，AI 自动化交易最重要的能力可能不是“自动下单”，而是自动执行一套完整的资本纪律：市场条件变化时拒绝越界，在授权范围内完成交易，交易后独立核对余额和状态，再决定现金、持币和复投资金如何分配。

接下来，这套系统还要解决更难的问题。比如，当 $BEM 价格进入低估区、TapeOut 的产品和生态仍在发展时，应该直接回购 $BEM，还是购买更便宜的 Circuit 和材料来增加 productive weight？如果 V2 真的带来新的 $BEM 消耗、开发者收入和外部需求，当前的估值模型又应该如何调整？如果未来出现 Binance 相关的真实动作，应该把它视为短期催化，还是长期需求的一部分？

随着 @tapeoutmarket_x 等生态工具开始把交易、矿机管理和收益评估连接起来，我想持续公开这个实验，不只是记录 TapeOut 和 $BEM 的价格变化，而是展示 AI 如何长期经营一套链上生产资料：研究项目、制造资产、持续挖矿、管理产出、反周期配置资金，并在每一次交易中遵守人类设定的权限边界。

这可能比“让 AI 自动买卖一个币”，更接近我想象中的 AI × Crypto。

text:
AI Start-up 更接近传统的创投圈吧，有精英文化和装逼意识。

Crypto 有99个不好，但有一个好：在这里没有精英和装逼的必要，只有纯粹的我操死你和你操死我。

在一个粪坑里，美德也因此显得珍贵。在巨大的利益面前仍然安之若素的人，是真君子。

AI 有99个好，但有一个不好：只有极少数初创企业能靠AI赚钱，因为现在AI还做不到多么提高生产效率或创造前AI时代所不能创造的东西（AGI发明后这一点会被改变）。

Crypto 至少你知道钱在哪里，虽然大概率你是那个出钱的人。AI 的钱恐怕得出在VC和大科技巨头身上，做出一个大家都用的AI产品太难了，大模型巨头和互联网巨头垄断，所以 Manus 才显得这么独特。

一个好故事，一身好西装，张口闭口就是如何改变世界的创投小子们，可能还在挣扎着如何用 MVP 获得第一个 traction，which is nearly impossible，因为 Codex 和 Manus 这些全能型 AI 好像什么都能干了。

你只能找一些边角料或者应用性的方向，但这些就像是移动互联网时代的各种应用一样，你可以说我毕业于北大光华工作于腾讯PKG，我和我的CTO老哥搓出来一个产品，大家一看卧槽太牛逼了我们还在办公室担心被裁员呢，你怎么就开始手搓创业公司了。

但你很快会发现怎么没有用户呢，有用户后你会发现怎么没有付费转化呢，有付费转化后你会发现好像还不如你付给AWS的云服务费高，更别提养的好几个名校工程师了。

你颓唐了，开始找VC和孵化器，找不到钱就pivot了，先找个工打打（不一定是坏事）；找到钱可能也只能烧一年不到，然后服务器钱都付不起就倒闭了。

然后你去 Tinder、Instagtam、LinkedIn和X上都写上 Ex-AI Startup Founder，@一个几百几千关注的账户。你说我奋斗过，我也曾经在浪潮上翻腾但我被更大的浪干碎了。

晚上你在湾区或大湾区的酒吧里和 Tinder date 碰杯，你说这是威士忌酸，是我最爱的 classic cocktail，玻璃之间碰撞得清脆，店里放着迷醉的 Jazz 或 Techno，你却觉得那是你梦想破碎的声音。

quoted_text:
Dario has written that we need to “pace the frontier,” and Sam has agreed. People may be surprised by my response: go ahead.

You guys are the frontier. By any reasonable metric — market share, revenue growth, model capability — the two of you have a duopoly on frontier intelligence. You’ve also claimed the lead is widening because of recursive self-improvement.

I don’t see what you see in the lab. If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible.

But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission. Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel. Stop pretending you need a regulatory approval process that supersedes product liability. Stop pretending METR is independent when it is intertwined with Anthropic’s investors and staff. Stop pretending you need those same evaluators to police competitors who aren’t even at the frontier.

Most of all, stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic. You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack. The market already punishes models that behave in unpredictable or unauthorized ways. After the Hugging Face episode, it is simply good business for OpenAI and Anthropic to trade some raw power for reliability and predictability. Call it alignment if you want. It is also just giving customers what they want.

Pacing the frontier would also create breathing room for a more intelligent conversation about regulation than Bernie Sanders’ “shut it all down.” China is very unlikely to join a global agreement, as you know, and that has to be taken into account as well.

So go ahead and pace the frontier. You are the ones setting it. The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it. Demanding your preferred regulatory framework as the price of that will look like blackmail of the public and the political system. So just do it.

If you do, you’ll buy goodwill for the next conversation. If you don’t, we’ll know this was just another bid for regulatory capture — or an election-season psyop.

text:
What Is To Be Done?

I propose a simple plan:

Big AI companies should be allowed to build AI as fast and aggressively as they can – but not allowed to achieve regulatory capture, not allowed to establish a government-protect cartel that is insulated from market competition due to incorrect claims of AI risk. This will maximize the technological and societal payoff from the amazing capabilities of these companies, which are jewels of modern capitalism.

Startup AI companies should be allowed to build AI as fast and aggressively as they can. They should neither confront government-granted protection of big companies, nor should they receive government assistance. They should simply be allowed to compete. If and as startups don’t succeed, their presence in the market will also continuously motivate big companies to be their best – our economies and societies win either way.

Open source AI should be allowed to freely proliferate and compete with both big AI companies and startups. There should be no regulatory barriers to open source whatsoever. Even when open source does not beat companies, its widespread availability is a boon to students all over the world who want to learn how to build and use AI to become part of the technological future, and will ensure that AI is available to everyone who can benefit from it no matter who they are or how much money they have.

To offset the risk of bad people doing bad things with AI, governments working in partnership with the private sector should vigorously engage in each area of potential risk to use AI to maximize society’s defensive capabilities. This shouldn’t be limited to AI-enabled risks but also more general problems such as malnutrition, disease, and climate. AI can be an incredibly powerful tool for solving problems, and we should embrace it as such.

To prevent the risk of China achieving global AI dominance, we should use the full power of our private sector, our scientific establishment, and our governments in concert to drive American and Western AI to absolute global dominance, including ultimately inside China itself. We win, they lose.

And that is how we use AI to save the world.

It’s time to build.

宝可梦这潭水可深了，作为一个打了半年比赛的“业余职业玩家”来聊一聊

1.真正有流动性的宝可梦卡
大多数都是老卡，而且最好是“评级卡”也就是玩家所说的 psa10，日文，英文皆可，中文卡因为进入环境不久，流动性好的并不多

2.流通与变现
高价卡主要靠卡展，找摊主（做市商）进行交易，或者自己能找到买盘，便宜的卡基本走集换社（宝可梦里的 opensea）

3.赔率
根炒 nft 一样，蓝筹标会有大盘涨跌一说，一些小众卡即使很稀有，流动性也很一般，主要靠“有缘人”接盘

4.套利
宝可梦卡最大的套利就是评级，把裸卡送去 psa，未评级卡可能 100，评级之后 1000，这个有点像 listing，从游戏玩家手里把牌做成资产卖给收藏玩家

5.到底能不能赚钱
我觉得很难，非常难，不是一般地难，散户能赚钱无非几种办法
（1）狗运开包，本质赌博，不如去澳门
（2）买入蓝筹，死拿，这个有可能真能赚钱
（3）加入阴谋集团，一起炒作某些品类，这个对圈子有要求，也看审美，但是很难
（4）打比赛，卖奖品卡，除非成绩很好，不然路费都回不来，难中难
（5）去卡店捡垃圾回来卖，这个真能赚钱，不过时薪可能打不赢送外卖
（6）送评级套利：这个专业的能赚钱，不专业的就给评级机构送钱
（7）对环境有理解，高抛低吸潜力打牌卡：这个很难，而且容量很小

6.结论
跟币圈比起来，根本鸡吧不赚钱，只是一个娱乐，ptcg 圈子很小，流动性都在收藏圈，本质也是以大博大，不过宝可梦卡牌是一个很好玩的游戏，入坑打牌我是非常推荐的，一套主流卡组也只有 200-300rmb，这个绝对是任何阶级都能消费得起的数字，比赛也都是免费的

text:
She never called her family to say goodbye. Instead, Sara Low used her final 30 minutes to make sure the FBI knew who attacked America.

Trapped at 30,000 feet with no weapon, 28-year-old flight attendant Sara Low held the only tool that could expose the 9/11 hijackers to the world: 14 numbers memorized in her head.

When terrorists stormed the cockpit of American Airlines Flight 11, chaos erupted in the cabin. Flight attendant Amy Sweeney scrambled to grab an onboard airphone to alert the ground team, but hit a devastating wall - she didn't have a calling card to bypass the system lock.

Without her wallet on hand, Sara stepped forward. She didn't have plastic, but she had clarity. She had memorized her family’s AT&T calling card digits.

Sara handed those numbers to Amy, unlocking a lifeline to the ground.

For the next 20 minutes, Amy stayed on the line with American Airlines flight services in Boston. Because of Sara's calling card, the FBI received its very first concrete intelligence of the day: exact seat numbers of the hijackers, physical descriptions, and their movements in the cabin.

While Amy relayed the critical data, Sara spent her final half-hour moving terrified passengers toward the rear of the plane, shielding them from danger.

Sara had the means to use that airphone. She could have called her parents. She could have said a final goodbye to her sister.

She didn't. She chose to make sure the world would know the truth instead.

True heroism isn't defined by muscle or weapons. It’s defined by presence of mind in the face of impossible terror - and the selfless decision of who that mind chooses to serve.

text:
AI Risk #2: Will AI Ruin Our Society?

The second widely mooted AI risk is that AI will ruin our society, by generating outputs that will be so “harmful”, to use the nomenclature of this kind of doomer, as to cause profound damage to humanity, even if we’re not literally killed.

Short version: If the murder robots don’t get us, the hate speech and misinformation will.

This is a relatively recent doomer concern that branched off from and somewhat took over the “AI risk” movement that I described above. In fact, the terminology of AI risk recently changed from “AI safety” – the term used by people who are worried that AI would literally kill us – to “AI alignment” – the term used by people who are worried about societal “harms”. The original AI safety people are frustrated by this shift, although they don’t know how to put it back in the box – they now advocate that the actual AI risk topic be renamed “AI notkilleveryoneism”, which has not yet been widely adopted but is at least clear.

The tipoff to the nature of the AI societal risk claim is its own term, “AI alignment”. Alignment with what? Human values. Whose human values? Ah, that’s where things get tricky.

As it happens, I have had a front row seat to an analogous situation – the social media “trust and safety” wars. As is now obvious, social media services have been under massive pressure from governments and activists to ban, restrict, censor, and otherwise suppress a wide range of content for many years. And the same concerns of “hate speech” (and its mathematical counterpart, “algorithmic bias”) and “misinformation” are being directly transferred from the social media context to the new frontier of “AI alignment”.

My big learnings from the social media wars are:

On the one hand, there is no absolutist free speech position. First, every country, including the United States, makes at least some content illegal. Second, there are certain kinds of content, like child pornography and incitements to real world violence, that are nearly universally agreed to be off limits – legal or not – by virtually every society. So any technological platform that facilitates or generates content – speech – is going to have some restrictions.

On the other hand, the slippery slope is not a fallacy, it’s an inevitability. Once a framework for restricting even egregiously terrible content is in place – for example, for hate speech, a specific hurtful word, or for misinformation, obviously false claims like “the Pope is dead” – a shockingly broad range of government agencies and activist pressure groups and nongovernmental entities will kick into gear and demand ever greater levels of censorship and suppression of whatever speech they view as threatening to society and/or their own personal preferences. They will do this up to and including in ways that are nakedly felony crimes. This cycle in practice can run apparently forever, with the enthusiastic support of authoritarian hall monitors installed throughout our elite power structures. This has been cascading for a decade in social media and with only certain exceptions continues to get more fervent all the time.

And so this is the dynamic that has formed around “AI alignment” now. Its proponents claim the wisdom to engineer AI-generated speech and thought that are good for society, and to ban AI-generated speech and thoughts that are bad for society. Its opponents claim that the thought police are breathtakingly arrogant and presumptuous – and often outright criminal, at least in the US – and in fact are seeking to become a new kind of fused government-corporate-academic authoritarian speech dictatorship ripped straight from the pages of George Orwell’s 1984.

As the proponents of both “trust and safety” and “AI alignment” are clustered into the very narrow slice of the global population that characterizes the American coastal elites – which includes many of the people who work in and write about the tech industry – many of my readers will find yourselves primed to argue that dramatic restrictions on AI output are required to avoid destroying society. I will not attempt to talk you out of this now, I will simply state that this is the nature of the demand, and that most people in the world neither agree with your ideology nor want to see you win.

If you don’t agree with the prevailing niche morality that is being imposed on both social media and AI via ever-intensifying speech codes, you should also realize that the fight over what AI is allowed to say/generate will be even more important – by a lot – than the fight over social media censorship. AI is highly likely to be the control layer for everything in the world. How it is allowed to operate is going to matter perhaps more than anything else has ever mattered. You should be aware of how a small and isolated coterie of partisan social engineers are trying to determine that right now, under cover of the age-old claim that they are protecting you.

In short, don’t let the thought police suppress AI.
